```{r blind-switch}
UNBLIND <- as.logical(Sys.getenv("UNBLIND_STUDY3", "FALSE"))
# The blind switch. UNBLIND is FALSE unless the environment variable
# UNBLIND_STUDY3 (a named setting the operating system passes to R) is set to
# TRUE. While it is FALSE, the source and stated-time labels are shuffled
# right after the data are built (section 3), and every output goes to a
# blind_run/ subfolder of the folder its real counterpart goes to. A value
# that is neither TRUE nor FALSE stops the run.
if (is.na(UNBLIND)) stop("UNBLIND_STUDY3 must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# A blind report belongs in blind_run/, and an unblinded report beside this
# file. The knit: line in the header reads the same environment variable and
# sends the report to the right folder when the file is knitted with
# RStudio's Knit button. A call to rmarkdown::render() must pass
# output_dir = "blind_run" in a blind run and leave it out in an unblinded
# run. A run whose report would land in the wrong folder stops here, before
# anything is written. The folder is read from the settings render() is
# running with; a knit that does not go through render() is not checked.
render_output_dir <- function() {
  frame <- Find(function(e) exists("output_dir", envir = e, inherits = FALSE) &&
                  exists("knit_input", envir = e, inherits = FALSE),
                sys.frames())
  if (is.null(frame)) return(NULL)
  d <- get("output_dir", envir = frame)
  normalizePath(if (is.null(d)) "." else d, mustWork = FALSE)
}
report_dir <- render_output_dir()
if (!UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) != "blind_run") {
  stop("A blind report must be written to blind_run/. Knit with the Knit ",
       "button, or run rmarkdown::render(\"Study3_01_Quant.Rmd\", ",
       "output_dir = \"blind_run\").")
}
if (UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) == "blind_run") {
  stop("An unblinded report must not be written to blind_run/. Set the ",
       "environment variable UNBLIND_STUDY3 to TRUE before knitting, or run ",
       "rmarkdown::render(\"Study3_01_Quant.Rmd\") without output_dir.")
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

```{r banner, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!UNBLIND) {
  cat("**Blind run. The source labels are shuffled across participants and",
      "the stated-time labels across each participant's images, so nothing",
      "in this report is a result.**\n")
} else {
  cat("**Unblinded run on the real source and stated-time labels.**\n")
}
```

# 0. What this file does

Study 3 asks whether telling participants that an artist prompted an AI
system lowers ratings because the label signals little work, or because
people discount the process itself. Only the first account predicts that
stated hours shrink the gap between the Human and AI conditions until it is
negligible at 100 hours. The registration
(`Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study3_AsPredicted.md`) is the
specification for everything below, and nothing this file computes beyond it
is presented as confirmatory.

The design crosses source (Human or AI, one per participant) with stated time
(under 1 hour, 10 hours or 100 hours, all three seen by each participant).
Each participant rates nine of ten images on creativity and on effort, three
images at each stated time, and writes a justification beside every rating.

This file:

1. reads the two Qualtrics exports and the survey file, and applies the
   registered exclusions in order (section 2);
2. scores each rating by its position on the answer scale and attaches the
   stated time of each image (section 2);
3. shuffles the labels in a blind run and writes the long data file, one row
   per participant, image and rating (section 3);
4. fits the registered models, tests, Holm family, estimated marginal means,
   equivalence tests, random-slope refit and decision rule (section 5);
5. checks each Holm verdict with a cumulative-link model (section 6);
6. records the status of every fit and the run (sections 7 and 8).

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. lme4 fits the
# mixed models, and lmerTest adds F tests with Satterthwaite degrees of
# freedom (an approximation to the degrees of freedom a test in a mixed model
# has). emmeans gives estimated marginal means (the model's predicted mean for
# each condition and time) and contrasts between them. ordinal fits the
# cumulative-link mixed models of section 6.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(ordinal)
})
```

## 1.2 Paths

```{r paths}
# Every path is found from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory when the file is knitted. Three environment variables override
# the defaults:
#   STUDY3_DIR           the Study 3 folder, where the outputs go
#   STUDY_SHARED_R       the folder of the shared R helpers
#   STUDY3_PROJECT_ROOT  the project root, the folder that holds Data and
#                        Analysis
# Printed paths are relative to the Study 3 folder or the project root, so no
# printed line names a folder particular to one machine.
STUDY_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STUDY3_DIR", getwd()), mustWork = TRUE)
SHARED_R  <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_R",
                        file.path(STUDY_DIR, "..", "shared", "R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "qualtrics_import.R"))

PROJECT_ROOT <- find_project_root(start = STUDY_DIR,
                                  env_var = "STUDY3_PROJECT_ROOT")
EXPORTS <- study_export_paths(PROJECT_ROOT, 3)

# A blind run writes each file to a blind_run/ subfolder of the folder its
# real counterpart goes to.
mode_dir <- function(dir) if (UNBLIND) dir else file.path(dir, "blind_run")
OUT_STUDY  <- mode_dir(STUDY_DIR)
OUT_TABLES <- mode_dir(file.path(STUDY_DIR, "tables"))
for (p in c(OUT_STUDY, OUT_TABLES)) {
  dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

cat("Values export: ", relative_path(EXPORTS$values, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Labels export: ", relative_path(EXPORTS$labels, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Survey file:   ", relative_path(EXPORTS$qsf, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Long data to:  ", relative_path(OUT_STUDY, STUDY_DIR), "\n")
cat("Tables to:     ", relative_path(OUT_TABLES, STUDY_DIR), "\n")

# The registered constants.
SEED       <- 20260421L   # the Study 1 seed, used for every shuffle
EQ_BOUND   <- 0.224       # half the 0.448-point Study 1 creativity penalty
ALPHA      <- 0.05
DIMS       <- c("creativity", "effort")
TYPE_LEVELS <- c("Human", "AI")
TIME_LEVELS <- c("under 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")
# The survey shows the shortest time as "less than 1 hour"; the registration
# calls it "under 1 hour".
TIME_FROM_SURVEY <- c("less than 1 hour" = "under 1 hour",
                      "10 hours"         = "10 hours",
                      "100 hours"        = "100 hours")
TASK_ANSWER <- "Viewing images for a set amount of time and answering questions"
```

## 1.3 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record ties every output to this run. It stores the SHA-256
# checksum of each input (a 64-character fingerprint of the file's exact
# bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest now, deletes each output's
# previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and writes the manifest last.
# A manifest on disk therefore means the run reached its end.
run <- start_run_record(
  c(values_export = EXPORTS$values,
    labels_export = EXPORTS$labels,
    survey_file   = EXPORTS$qsf),
  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_quant_run_manifest.csv"),
  STUDY_DIR)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_quant_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")
print(as.data.frame(run$inputs[, c("input", "file", "bytes", "sha256")]))

if (!UNBLIND) {
  # A short note in each blind folder says what the folder holds.
  blind_notes <- file.path(c(OUT_STUDY, OUT_TABLES), "BLIND_RUN.txt")
  run_clear_outputs(run, blind_notes)
  for (f in blind_notes) {
    writeLines(c(
      "Outputs of a blind run of the Study 3 pipeline.",
      "The source labels were shuffled across participants, and the stated-time",
      "labels across each participant's images, before any summary or model.",
      "Study3_03_Integration.Rmd also shuffles the ratings across the responses",
      "to each question before it relates any word to a rating. No number in",
      "this folder describes the real conditions or the real link between the",
      "words and the ratings. A run with UNBLIND_STUDY3 set to TRUE writes the",
      "real outputs one folder up."), f)
  }
}
```

# 2. Import and exclusions

## 2.1 The exclusion flow

```{r exclusions}
# Qualtrics, the survey platform, exports the study twice: the Values export
# holds raw choice codes and the Labels export holds the text each
# participant saw. read_qualtrics_pair() reads both and checks that they hold
# the same records in the same order.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_exclusion_flow.csv"))

ex <- read_qualtrics_pair(EXPORTS$values, EXPORTS$labels)
stopifnot(all(trim_answer(ex$labels$Status) %in% c("IP Address", "Survey Preview")))

# The registered steps, in the order of registration question 6. Each step
# returns TRUE for the records it keeps. Survey Preview records are the
# survey test runs. A blank seriousness answer counts as an answer other than
# "Yes, I did". No arithmetic answer is blank by the fourth step, and the
# step stops if one is, so a blank never has to be read as right or wrong.
steps <- list(
  "survey test runs (Status is Survey Preview)" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Status) == "IP Address",
  "unfinished records" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Finished) == "True",
  "seriousness answer other than Yes, I did (blanks included)" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Seriousness) == "Yes, I did",
  "wrong answer to What does 8+7 equal?" =
    function(v, l) {
      a <- trim_answer(l$AttentionCheck2)
      if (any(a == "")) stop("A record reaching the arithmetic step has no answer.")
      a == "15"
    }
)
flow <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps)

# One line per step, so the flow can be read off the report.
ff <- flow$flow
cat("Records in the export:", ff$n[1], "\n")
for (i in 2:nrow(ff)) {
  cat(sprintf("Step %d, %s: %d -> %d (%d removed)\n",
              i - 1, ff$step[i], ff$n[i - 1], ff$n[i], ff$removed[i]))
}

# The counts the registration states. The run stops if the exports give
# anything else.
REGISTERED_FLOW <- c(100L, 96L, 94L, 87L, 85L)
ff$registered_n <- REGISTERED_FLOW
if (!identical(as.integer(ff$n), REGISTERED_FLOW)) {
  stop("The exclusion flow does not match the registration: ",
       paste(ff$n, collapse = " -> "), " against ",
       paste(REGISTERED_FLOW, collapse = " -> "), ".")
}
write_csv(ff, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_exclusion_flow.csv"))

# The registration states that the 85 records left all have a recorded
# condition and a correct answer to the task question.
type_kept <- trim_answer(flow$labels$Type)
stopifnot(all(type_kept %in% TYPE_LEVELS),
          all(trim_answer(flow$labels$AttentionCheck) == TASK_ANSWER))
```

## 2.2 Scoring by position

```{r scoring}
# Each rating is scored 1 to 5 by the position of its label among the
# item's answer options, read from the survey file in the order they were
# shown, because the numeric export stores raw choice codes (1, 2, 3, 6 and 7
# on 1FigureEff). An answer whose label is not among the item's current
# options is scored NA and listed in the log.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_item_scales.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_unscored_answers.csv"))

scales <- read_item_scales(EXPORTS$qsf, ITEM_FAMILIES$original$pattern)
stopifnot(nrow(scales) == 20, all(scales$k == 5))
write_csv(select(scales, item, question_id, k, anchors, stem),
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_item_scales.csv"))
cat("Rating items:", nrow(scales), "| answer options per item:",
    paste(unique(scales$k), collapse = ", "), "\n")

built <- reshape_ratings_long(flow$values, flow$labels, scales, "original",
                              carry_labels = "Type")

# The registration names two 1FigureEff answers with a code absent from the
# final survey. They are the only unscored answers.
unscored <- built$unscored
print(as.data.frame(unscored))
stopifnot(nrow(unscored) == 1, unscored$item == "1FigureEff",
          unscored$label == "5", unscored$n == 2)
write_csv(unscored, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_unscored_answers.csv"))
```

## 2.3 The stated time of each image

```{r stated-times}
# The survey script records the image shown in each of nine slots (Image1 to
# Image9) and the time stated for it (Image1_Time to Image9_Time). An image
# field such as Image3_Nonfigure names the third non-figurative image, whose
# rating items are tagged 3NonFigure.
image_slots <- bind_rows(lapply(1:9, function(k) {
  tibble(id         = flow$labels$ResponseId,
         slot       = k,
         image      = trim_answer(flow$labels[[paste0("Image", k)]]),
         time_label = trim_answer(flow$labels[[paste0("Image", k, "_Time")]]))
}))
parts <- regmatches(image_slots$image,
                    regexec("^Image([1-5])_(Figure|Nonfigure)$", image_slots$image))
if (any(lengths(parts) != 3)) {
  stop("Some image field does not name one of the ten images.")
}
if (!all(image_slots$time_label %in% names(TIME_FROM_SURVEY))) {
  stop("Some stated time is not one of the three registered times.")
}
image_slots <- image_slots %>%
  mutate(stimulus_id = paste0(vapply(parts, `[`, "", 2),
                              ifelse(vapply(parts, `[`, "", 3) == "Figure",
                                     "Figure", "NonFigure")),
         time = unname(TIME_FROM_SURVEY[time_label]))

# Each participant saw nine different images, three at each stated time.
per_person <- image_slots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_images = n_distinct(stimulus_id),
            n_under1 = sum(time == "under 1 hour"),
            n_10     = sum(time == "10 hours"),
            n_100    = sum(time == "100 hours"), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(per_person) == 85, all(per_person$n_images == 9),
          all(per_person$n_under1 == 3), all(per_person$n_10 == 3),
          all(per_person$n_100 == 3))
cat("Every participant saw 9 images, 3 at each stated time.\n")
```

## 2.4 The long data and the registered counts

```{r long-data}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_sample_checks.csv"))

# One row per participant, image and rating dimension. A row exists when the
# participant gave a rating or a justification. The stated time comes from
# the image's slot, and every rated image must be one of the nine listed.
long <- built$long %>%
  left_join(select(image_slots, id, stimulus_id, time),
            by = c("id", "stimulus_id"), relationship = "many-to-one")
if (anyNA(long$time)) stop("Some rated image is not among the nine listed.")
if (nrow(anti_join(image_slots, long, by = c("id", "stimulus_id"))) > 0) {
  stop("Some listed image has no rating and no justification.")
}

long <- long %>%
  transmute(id, Type, time,
            stimulus_type, stimulus_num = as.integer(image), stimulus_id,
            dimension, rating, response_text = justification,
            item, k_points, rating_label, raw_choice_id)

# The counts the registration states, beside the counts the data give. A
# recorded rating is an answer the participant chose, scored or not; three
# participants left one rating blank, and the two answers with an absent code
# are recorded but not scored.
ratings_per_person <- long %>% group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_recorded = sum(raw_choice_id != ""), .groups = "drop")
participants <- distinct(long, id, Type)
sample_checks <- tribble(
  ~quantity,                                  ~registered, ~observed,
  "participants",                             85L, nrow(participants),
  "participants in the Human condition",      43L, sum(participants$Type == "Human"),
  "participants in the AI condition",         42L, sum(participants$Type == "AI"),
  "justifications",                           1530L, sum(long$response_text != ""),
  "ratings",                                  1525L, sum(!is.na(long$rating)),
  "participants with 17 recorded ratings",    3L, sum(ratings_per_person$n_recorded == 17),
  "participants with 18 recorded ratings",    82L, sum(ratings_per_person$n_recorded == 18),
  "1FigureEff answers with an absent code",   2L, sum(unscored$n)
) %>% mutate(match = registered == observed)
print(as.data.frame(sample_checks))
write_csv(sample_checks, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_sample_checks.csv"))
if (!all(sample_checks$match)) stop("The sample does not match the registration.")
stopifnot(nrow(long) == 85 * 9 * 2)
```

# 3. The blind shuffle and the long data file

```{r blind-shuffle}
# In a blind run the labels are shuffled here, after the data are built and
# before any summary or model.
#
# Source is a between-participant label. blind_shuffle() deals each
# participant another participant's source label, so each condition keeps
# its 43 or 42 participants.
#
# Stated time varies within each participant, so it is shuffled within each
# participant: the participant's nine time labels are dealt again among the
# same nine images, each image keeping one time for both its ratings. Every
# participant keeps three images at each time, and the link between an
# image's stated time and its ratings is cut.
#
# Both shuffles use the registered seed, take participants and images in byte
# order of their identifiers so the result is the same on every machine, and
# put the random-number state back afterwards.
shuffle_time_within <- function(df, seed) {
  units <- distinct(df, id, stimulus_id, time)
  if (anyDuplicated(units[, c("id", "stimulus_id")]) > 0) {
    stop("Some image carries more than one stated time.")
  }
  units <- units[order(units$id, units$stimulus_id, method = "radix"), ]
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit({
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
    else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  }, add = TRUE)
  set.seed(seed)
  rows_by_id <- split(seq_len(nrow(units)),
                      factor(units$id, levels = sort(unique(units$id), method = "radix")))
  new_time <- character(nrow(units))
  for (rows in rows_by_id) {
    new_time[rows] <- units$time[rows][sample.int(length(rows))]
  }
  units$time <- new_time
  out <- df
  key <- match(paste(out$id, out$stimulus_id), paste(units$id, units$stimulus_id))
  out$time <- units$time[key]
  out
}

if (!UNBLIND) {
  long <- blind_shuffle(long, "id", "Type", seed = SEED)
  long <- shuffle_time_within(long, seed = SEED)
  # The design survives the shuffle: 43 and 42 participants, and three
  # images per participant at each time.
  stopifnot(identical(sort(table(distinct(long, id, Type)$Type)),
                      sort(table(participants$Type))))
  stopifnot(all(table(distinct(long, id, stimulus_id, time)[, c("id", "time")]) == 3))
  cat("Blind run: source labels shuffled across participants, stated-time",
      "labels shuffled within each participant, seed", SEED, "\n")
}

long <- long %>%
  mutate(Type = factor(Type, levels = TYPE_LEVELS),
         time = factor(time, levels = TIME_LEVELS),
         dimension = factor(dimension, levels = DIMS)) %>%
  arrange(id, stimulus_id, dimension)
stopifnot(!anyNA(long$Type), !anyNA(long$time))
```

```{r write-long}
# The long data file is the input of Study3_02_Text.ipynb, which reads only
# its identifier, image, dimension and text columns, and of
# Study3_03_Integration.Rmd. It carries the condition and the rating, so in a
# blind run it is written to blind_run/ with the shuffled labels. Missing
# values are written as empty cells.
LONG_PATH <- file.path(OUT_STUDY, "study3_long_with_text.csv")
run_clear_outputs(run, LONG_PATH)
write_csv(long, LONG_PATH, na = "")
cat("Wrote", relative_path(LONG_PATH, STUDY_DIR), "with", nrow(long), "rows.\n")
```

```{r cell-counts}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_cell_counts.csv"))
cell_counts <- long %>%
```

# 5. The registered models

## 5.1 The fits

```{r fit-models}
# Each rating gets a linear mixed model, a regression with its own baseline
# for each participant and each image:
#
#   rating ~ source x time + (1 | participant) + (1 | image)
#
# with time a three-level factor. Both factors use sum-to-zero contrasts, a
# coding in which a factor's effects add to zero across its levels, so the
# test of each factor is its effect averaged over the levels of the other.
# The fit is by restricted maximum likelihood (REML, the usual estimator of
# the variances in a mixed model) with the bobyqa optimizer, as in Study 1.
# fit_with_status() keeps every warning and records whether the fit
# converged and whether it is singular (a variance estimated at zero or a
# correlation at plus or minus one).
model_data <- function(dim) {
  d <- long %>%
    filter(dimension == dim, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(id = factor(id), stimulus_id = factor(stimulus_id))
  contrasts(d$Type) <- contr.sum(2)
  contrasts(d$time) <- contr.sum(3)
  d
}
FORMULA_PRIMARY <- rating ~ Type * time + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)
FORMULA_SLOPES  <- rating ~ Type * time + (1 + time | id) + (1 + Type | stimulus_id)

data_by_dim <- setNames(lapply(DIMS, model_data), DIMS)
primary <- lapply(data_by_dim, function(d) {
  fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(FORMULA_PRIMARY, data = d, REML = TRUE,
                                 control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
})
for (dim in DIMS) {
  st <- primary[[dim]]$status
  cat(dim, ": rows", nrow(data_by_dim[[dim]]), "| fit error", st$fit_error,
      "| converged", st$converged, "| singular", st$singular, "\n")
}
```

## 5.2 F tests and the Holm family

```{r f-tests}
# Source, time and their interaction get F tests with Satterthwaite degrees
# of freedom, from the type III table (each term tested with the others in
# the model), which under sum-to-zero contrasts averages each main effect
# over the other factor. emmeans::joint_tests() computes the same three
# tests from the estimated marginal means and reports each F value rounded to
# three decimals, and the table records that the two agree to that rounding.
# Holm's method corrects the six tests together: the p-values
# are ordered, the smallest is compared with .05 divided by six, the next
# with .05 divided by five, and so on, stopping at the first that fails. This
# holds the chance of any false positive in the six at .05.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_lmm_ftests.csv"))

TERM_NAMES <- c("Type" = "source", "time" = "stated time",
                "Type:time" = "source by stated time")

ftests <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(dim) {
  res <- primary[[dim]]
  if (res$status$fit_error) {
    return(tibble(dimension = dim, term = names(TERM_NAMES),
                  effect = unname(TERM_NAMES), F = NA_real_, num_df = NA_real_,
                  den_df = NA_real_, p_raw = NA_real_,
                  F_joint_tests = NA_real_, F_agrees = NA,
                  note = fit_note(res$status)))
  }
  a  <- anova(res$fit, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite")
  jt <- as.data.frame(emmeans::joint_tests(res$fit, lmer.df = "satterthwaite"))
  f_jt <- jt$F.ratio[match(names(TERM_NAMES),
                           gsub(" ", "", jt$`model term`))]
  tibble(dimension = dim,
         term      = names(TERM_NAMES),
         effect    = unname(TERM_NAMES),
         F         = a[names(TERM_NAMES), "F value"],
         num_df    = a[names(TERM_NAMES), "NumDF"],
         den_df    = a[names(TERM_NAMES), "DenDF"],
         p_raw     = a[names(TERM_NAMES), "Pr(>F)"],
         F_joint_tests = f_jt) %>%
    mutate(F_agrees = abs(F - F_joint_tests) <= 6e-4,
           p_raw = na_unless_usable(p_raw, res$status),
           note  = fit_note(res$status))
}))
ftests <- ftests %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm", n = nrow(ftests)),
         holm_family = "six tests: source, stated time and their interaction, on both ratings",
         survives_holm = p_holm < ALPHA,
         model = "rating ~ Type * time + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), sum-to-zero contrasts, REML, bobyqa; type III F tests, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom") %>%
  relocate(p_holm, survives_holm, .after = p_raw)
stopifnot(all(ftests$F_agrees, na.rm = TRUE))
write_csv(ftests, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_lmm_ftests.csv"))
cat("The type III and joint-test F values agree on every term:",
    all(ftests$F_agrees), "\n")
print(as.data.frame(select(ftests, dimension, effect, F, num_df, den_df,
                           p_raw, p_holm, survives_holm)), digits = 4)
```

## 5.3 Estimated marginal means

```{r emmeans}
# From each fit: the predicted mean for each source and time; the Human
# minus AI gap at each time, with its 95 percent confidence interval (the
# range of gaps compatible with the data); and the 100 hours minus under 1
# hour contrast averaged over source. Degrees of freedom are Satterthwaite's.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_emmeans_cells.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_gap_by_time.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_time_contrast.csv"))

gap_contrast <- function(fit) {
  contrast(emmeans(fit, ~ Type | time, lmer.df = "satterthwaite"),
           method = list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)), adjust = "none")
}
time_contrast <- function(fit) {
  contrast(emmeans(fit, ~ time, lmer.df = "satterthwaite"),
           method = list("100 hours minus under 1 hour" = c(-1, 0, 1)),
           adjust = "none")
}

emm_cells <- gaps <- time_contrasts <- list()
for (dim in DIMS) {
  res <- primary[[dim]]
  if (res$status$fit_error) next
  usable_cols <- function(tab) {
    tab %>% mutate(across(any_of(c("lower.CL", "upper.CL", "p.value")),
                          ~ na_unless_usable(.x, res$status)),
                   note = fit_note(res$status))
  }
  emm_cells[[dim]] <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans(res$fit, ~ Type * time,
                                                lmer.df = "satterthwaite"))) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim, .before = 1) %>% usable_cols()
  gaps[[dim]] <- as_tibble(summary(gap_contrast(res$fit),
                                   infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95)) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim, .before = 1) %>% usable_cols()
  time_contrasts[[dim]] <- as_tibble(summary(time_contrast(res$fit),
                                             infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95)) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim, averaged_over = "source, equal weights",
           .before = 1) %>% usable_cols()
}
emm_cells      <- bind_rows(emm_cells)
gaps           <- bind_rows(gaps)
time_contrasts <- bind_rows(time_contrasts)
write_csv(emm_cells, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_emmeans_cells.csv"))
write_csv(gaps, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_gap_by_time.csv"))
write_csv(time_contrasts, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_time_contrast.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(gaps, dimension, time, estimate, SE, df,
                           lower.CL, upper.CL)), digits = 4)
print(as.data.frame(select(time_contrasts, dimension, contrast, estimate, SE,
                           df, lower.CL, upper.CL)), digits = 4)
```

## 5.4 Equivalence at 100 hours, and the random-slope refit

```{r equivalence}
# On each rating, the 100-hour gap passes the equivalence test (two
# one-sided tests, each asking whether the gap lies on the near side of one
# bound) when its 90 percent confidence interval lies inside plus or minus
# 0.224 rating points. The table also gives the two one-sided tests' p-value
# from emmeans, which is below .05 exactly when the interval lies inside the
# bounds.
#
# The test must also pass in a refit with random slopes, which let the effect
# of source differ from image to image and the effect of time differ from
# participant to participant:
#
#   rating ~ source x time + (1 + time | participant) + (1 + source | image)
#
# unless that fit cannot estimate all its variance terms. Here that means the
# fit stopped with an error, did not converge, or is singular; the
# requirement is then waived, and the table says so.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_equivalence.csv"))

slopes <- lapply(data_by_dim, function(d) {
  fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(FORMULA_SLOPES, data = d, REML = TRUE,
                                 control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
                                                       optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))))
})

estimable <- function(status) {
  !isTRUE(status$fit_error) && isTRUE(status$converged) && !isTRUE(status$singular)
}

equivalence_row <- function(res, dim, fit_label) {
  base <- tibble(dimension = dim, fit = fit_label,
                 fit_error = res$status$fit_error,
                 converged = res$status$converged,
                 singular  = res$status$singular,
                 estimable = estimable(res$status))
  if (res$status$fit_error) {
    return(base %>% mutate(gap_100 = NA_real_, std_error = NA_real_,
                           df = NA_real_, ci90_low = NA_real_,
                           ci90_high = NA_real_, tost_p = NA_real_,
                           passes = NA, note = fit_note(res$status)))
  }
  g    <- gap_contrast(res$fit)
  ci90 <- as_tibble(summary(g, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE), level = 0.90)) %>%
    filter(time == "100 hours")
  tost <- as_tibble(summary(test(g, delta = EQ_BOUND, side = "equivalence"))) %>%
    filter(time == "100 hours")
  base %>% mutate(
    gap_100   = ci90$estimate,
    std_error = ci90$SE,
    df        = ci90$df,
    ci90_low  = na_unless_usable(ci90$lower.CL, res$status),
    ci90_high = na_unless_usable(ci90$upper.CL, res$status),
    tost_p    = na_unless_usable(tost$p.value, res$status),
    passes    = na_unless_usable(ci90$lower.CL > -EQ_BOUND &
                                   ci90$upper.CL < EQ_BOUND, res$status),
    note      = fit_note(res$status))
}

equivalence <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(dim) {
  bind_rows(equivalence_row(primary[[dim]], dim, "registered model"),
            equivalence_row(slopes[[dim]], dim, "random-slope refit"))
})) %>%
  mutate(bound = EQ_BOUND,
         tost_agrees_with_interval = (tost_p < ALPHA) == passes,
         rule = "passes when the 90 percent interval of the Human minus AI gap at 100 hours lies inside plus or minus the bound")
write_csv(equivalence, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_equivalence.csv"))
stopifnot(all(equivalence$tost_agrees_with_interval, na.rm = TRUE))
for (dim in DIMS) {
  st <- slopes[[dim]]$status
  cat(dim, "random-slope refit: fit error", st$fit_error, "| converged",
      st$converged, "| singular", st$singular, "| estimable",
      estimable(st), "\n")
}
print(as.data.frame(select(equivalence, dimension, fit, estimable, gap_100,
                           ci90_low, ci90_high, tost_p, passes)), digits = 4)
```

## 5.5 The decision rule

```{r decision}
# The registered rule, on each rating.
#
#   time closes the gap  the interaction survives the Holm correction, the
#                        Human minus AI gap is smaller at 100 hours than at
#                        under 1 hour, and the equivalence test passes;
#   the gap persists     the equivalence test fails and the 95 percent
#                        interval of the gap at 100 hours lies above zero;
#   inconclusive         any other pattern.
#
# The equivalence test passes when it passes in the registered model and
# either passes in the random-slope refit or that refit cannot estimate all
# its variance terms. "Smaller" compares the two Human minus AI estimates as
# signed numbers. A rating whose registered fit is not usable gets no
# verdict.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_decision.csv"))

decision <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(dim) {
  res  <- primary[[dim]]
  inter <- filter(ftests, dimension == dim, term == "Type:time")
  g     <- filter(gaps, dimension == dim)
  eq_p  <- filter(equivalence, dimension == dim, fit == "registered model")
  eq_s  <- filter(equivalence, dimension == dim, fit == "random-slope refit")
  usable <- fit_usable(res$status)
  if (!usable || nrow(g) == 0) {
    return(tibble(dimension = dim, verdict = NA_character_,
                  note = fit_note(res$status, what = "verdict")))
  }
  slope_applies <- isTRUE(eq_s$estimable)
  tibble(
    dimension = dim,
    interaction_p_holm   = inter$p_holm,
    interaction_survives = inter$survives_holm,
    gap_under_1_hour     = g$estimate[g$time == "under 1 hour"],
    gap_100_hours        = g$estimate[g$time == "100 hours"],
    gap_smaller_at_100   = gap_100_hours < gap_under_1_hour,
    equivalence_registered = eq_p$passes,
    slope_requirement    = if (slope_applies) "applies" else
      paste0("waived: the random-slope refit ",
             if (isTRUE(eq_s$fit_error)) "stopped with an error"
             else if (!isTRUE(eq_s$converged)) "did not converge"
             else "is singular",
             ", so it cannot estimate all its variance terms"),
    equivalence_slopes   = eq_s$passes,
    equivalence_passes   = eq_p$passes & (if (slope_applies) eq_s$passes else TRUE),
    gap_100_ci95_low     = g$lower.CL[g$time == "100 hours"],
    gap_100_ci95_high    = g$upper.CL[g$time == "100 hours"],
    ci95_above_zero      = gap_100_ci95_low > 0
  ) %>%
    mutate(verdict = case_when(
      interaction_survives & gap_smaller_at_100 & equivalence_passes ~
        "time closes the gap",
      !equivalence_passes & ci95_above_zero ~ "the gap persists",
      TRUE ~ "inconclusive"),
      note = fit_note(res$status, what = "verdict"))
}))
write_csv(decision, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_decision.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(decision, dimension, verdict, slope_requirement)))
```

```{r study5-contrast}

# under 1 hour contrast of the registered model. This table carries that
# contrast and its standard error. A blind run's table is marked not usable,
# because its labels are shuffled.
STUDY5_PATH <- file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_time_contrast_for_study5.csv")
run_clear_outputs(run, STUDY5_PATH)
tc_creativity <- filter(time_contrasts, dimension == "creativity")
res_creativity <- primary[["creativity"]]
study5_contrast <- tibble(

  run_id     = run$run_id,

  usable     = UNBLIND && fit_usable(res_creativity$status),
  note       = if (!UNBLIND) {

  } else fit_note(res_creativity$status, what = "estimate")
)
write_csv(study5_contrast, STUDY5_PATH)
cat("Wrote", relative_path(STUDY5_PATH, STUDY_DIR), "| usable:",
    study5_contrast$usable, "\n")
```

# 6. The cumulative-link check of each Holm verdict

```{r clmm}
# A cumulative-link mixed model treats the five answers as ordered
# categories: it estimates where the cut points between adjacent answers
# fall on a latent scale instead of assuming the answers are evenly spaced.
# Each rating gets the registered model in that form, with the logit link (a
# logistic curve for the chance of answering above each cut point) and the
# same sum-to-zero contrasts:
#
#   ordered rating ~ source x time + (1 | participant) + (1 | image)
#
# Each term is tested by a Wald test (the squared estimates weighed against
# their covariance, compared with a chi-square distribution), which under
# sum-to-zero contrasts tests the effect averaged over the other factor. The
# six p-values are corrected by Holm, and each verdict (survives the
# correction or not) is set beside the linear model's.
#
# A fit counts as converged when the optimizer returns code 0 and raises no
# warning about convergence, the Hessian (the matrix of second derivatives
# the standard errors come from) or singularity, as in Study 1. It counts as
# singular when a random-effect standard deviation lies below 1e-4.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_clmm_check.csv"))

fit_clmm <- function(d) {
  d$rating_ord <- factor(d$rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE)
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(ordinal::clmm(rating_ord ~ Type * time + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
                           data = d, link = "logit", Hess = TRUE),
             error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  failed <- inherits(fit, "error")
  status <- tibble(
    fit_error = failed,
    converged = !failed && isTRUE(fit$optRes$convergence == 0) &&
      !any(grepl("converge|Hessian|singular", warns, ignore.case = TRUE)),
    singular  = if (failed) NA else
      any(vapply(ordinal::VarCorr(fit), function(m) any(attr(m, "stddev") < 1e-4),
                 logical(1))),
    lme4_messages = paste(unique(c(if (failed) conditionMessage(fit), warns)),
                          collapse = " | "))
  list(fit = fit, data = d, status = status,
       max_abs_gradient = if (failed) NA_real_ else max(abs(fit$gradient)))
}

wald_terms <- function(cl) {
  if (cl$status$fit_error) {
    return(tibble(term = names(TERM_NAMES), chisq = NA_real_, df = NA_integer_,
                  p_raw = NA_real_))
  }
  X <- model.matrix(~ Type * time, data = cl$data)
  assign <- attr(X, "assign")[-1]
  labels <- attr(terms(~ Type * time), "term.labels")
  beta <- cl$fit$beta
  stopifnot(identical(names(beta), colnames(X)[-1]))
  V <- vcov(cl$fit)[names(beta), names(beta)]
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(labels), function(t) {
    idx <- which(assign == t)
    w <- as.numeric(t(beta[idx]) %*% solve(V[idx, idx, drop = FALSE]) %*% beta[idx])
    tibble(term = labels[t], chisq = w, df = length(idx),
           p_raw = pchisq(w, length(idx), lower.tail = FALSE))
  }))
}

clmm_fits <- lapply(data_by_dim, fit_clmm)
clmm_check <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(dim) {
  cl <- clmm_fits[[dim]]
  wald_terms(cl) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim, .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(effect = unname(TERM_NAMES[term]),
           p_raw = na_unless_usable(p_raw, cl$status),
           clmm_converged = cl$status$converged,
           clmm_singular  = cl$status$singular,
           max_abs_gradient = cl$max_abs_gradient,
           note = fit_note(cl$status))
})) %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm", n = 2 * length(TERM_NAMES)),
         clmm_survives_holm = p_holm < ALPHA) %>%
  left_join(select(ftests, dimension, term, lmm_p_holm = p_holm,
                   lmm_survives_holm = survives_holm),
            by = c("dimension", "term")) %>%
  mutate(verdicts_agree = clmm_survives_holm == lmm_survives_holm,
         model = "ordered rating ~ Type * time + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), logit link, Laplace approximation, sum-to-zero contrasts; Wald chi-square test of each term") %>%
  relocate(effect, .after = term)
write_csv(clmm_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_clmm_check.csv"))
for (dim in DIMS) {
  cl <- clmm_fits[[dim]]
  cat(dim, "cumulative-link fit: fit error", cl$status$fit_error,
      "| converged", cl$status$converged, "| singular", cl$status$singular,
      "| largest absolute gradient", signif(cl$max_abs_gradient, 3), "\n")
}
print(as.data.frame(select(clmm_check, dimension, effect, p_raw, p_holm,
                           clmm_survives_holm, lmm_survives_holm,
                           verdicts_agree)), digits = 4)
```

# 7. Fit status

```{r fit-status}
# One row per fit in this file: the registered model, the random-slope refit
# and the cumulative-link model, on each rating.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_fit_status.csv"))
status_row <- function(status, dim, role, formula) {
  status %>% mutate(dimension = dim, role = role, formula = formula,
                    usable = fit_usable(status), .before = 1)
}
fit_status <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(dim) {
  bind_rows(
    status_row(primary[[dim]]$status, dim, "registered model",
               deparse1(FORMULA_PRIMARY)),
    status_row(slopes[[dim]]$status, dim, "random-slope refit",
               deparse1(FORMULA_SLOPES)),
    status_row(clmm_fits[[dim]]$status, dim, "cumulative-link check",
               "ordered rating ~ Type * time + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)"))
}))
print(as.data.frame(select(fit_status, dimension, role, fit_error, converged,
                           singular, usable)))
write_csv(fit_status, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study3_fit_status.csv"))
```
